language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
My name is Amber. I want to become a wizard.
Therefore I must earn 4 stars for my Wizard hat.
Today I'm exploring the magical canyon of chance. Here I will face 4 challenges that are each worth a star.
Look at this flower garden. I want to pick a flower with my eyes closed.
There are 3 pink flowers and 7 green flowers.
It is more likely to pick a green flower than a pink flower.
And the exact chance I pick a pink flower is 3 out of 10!
Help Amber with these games, so she can earn stars for her Wizard hat!

I want to determine the chance that the dragon will blow smoke instead of fire out of the dragon’s cave.

helperSimple.text: Look at Amber’s statements. Are they true or false?

activities.title: Is this statement true or false?
activities.subtitle: There is a 50/50 chance that the dragon will blow smoke or fire. When Amber sees the dragon 10 times, it is likely that 5 times she sees fire.

activities.title: Is this statement true or false?
activities.subtitle: There is a 50/50 chance that the dragon will blow smoke or fire. Amber has a 1 in 2 chance of seeing fire come out of the dragon.

activities.title: Is this statement true or false?
activities.subtitle: There is a 50/50 chance that the dragon will blow smoke or fire. When Amber sees the dragon 80 times, it is likely that 20 times she sees fire.

activities.title: Is this statement true or false?
activities.subtitle: There is a 50/50 chance that the dragon will blow smoke or fire. When Amber sees the dragon 5 times, it is likely that all 5 times she sees fire.

activities.title: Is this statement true or false?
activities.subtitle: There is a 50/50 chance that the dragon will blow smoke or fire. Amber can accurately predict each time whether the dragon will blow smoke or fire.

outro.text: Thank you! I have been awarded one star for my wizard hat!
